# Review recent activity table headers and row structure

> Prove the recent activity feed renders the required six-column table structure for portfolio events.

## Step 1

Open {{start_url}} in the browser and arrive at the dashboard view that contains the full-width Recent Activity section.

## Step 2

In the Recent Activity section, identify the table header row and read the visible column labels from left to right.

## Step 3

Assert the visible Recent Activity headers exactly match TIME, TYPE, DESCRIPTION, ASSET, VALUE, and STATUS in that order.

## Step 4 — assert @verifies ac-116

Confirm absolute check: TIME,TYPE,DESCRIPTION,ASSET,VALUE,STATUS (equals) — the stated promise: The recent activity table shows exactly these column headers: TIME, TYPE, DESCRIPTION, ASSET, VALUE, and STATUS.

content.test_md_blob:
# Review recent activity status pill rendering

> Prove visible recent-activity statuses are rendered as compact pill-style labels.

## Step 1

Open {{start_url}} in the browser and arrive at the dashboard view that contains the full-width Recent Activity section.

## Step 2

In the Recent Activity table, inspect each visible STATUS cell for the rows currently shown in the feed.

## Step 3

Assert every visible STATUS value is shown inside a compact pill-style badge rather than as plain uncontained text.

## Step 4 — assert @verifies ac-117

Confirm presence check: every visible STATUS value is shown inside a compact pill-style badge (forall) — the stated promise: Each displayed status is rendered as a pill-style label in the STATUS column.

judgements.rationale: [value_score] Scored highest for retention because the column schema is the primary interpretation contract of the Recent Activity feed and the source states it unambiguously.
[value_score] Scored second because compact pill rendering is explicitly promised and materially affects scanability, but it is narrower than the table-structure contract.
[applicability] Applicable and verified in t1 because this scenario exists to prove the exact Recent Activity header contract.
[applicability] Not applicable because the table-structure scenario does not need to prove status styling to validate the header contract.
[applicability] Not applicable because the status-presentation scenario is intentionally narrower than the full column-schema promise.
[applicability] Applicable and verified in t2 because this scenario exists to prove pill-style rendering of visible statuses.

[self_critique] Oracle-proof check passed: an exact header equality assertion directly proves ac-116. Technique fit passed: a happy-path visual inspection matches a fixed structural UI promise. Negative-case review found no source-backed invalid-input or alternate-outcome behavior to test without guessing. Over-breadth review passed after limiting the scope to visible Recent Activity headers only, not unstated row data or ordering.

[self_critique] Oracle-proof check passed: a forall presence check over visible STATUS cells directly proves ac-117. Technique fit passed: a happy-path rendered-surface inspection matches the styling promise. Negative-case review found no source-backed contrary status-style behavior to test without inventing unsupported states. Over-breadth review passed after scoping the assertion to visible rows only and not claiming specific status vocabulary or feed ordering.
